newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican leftist rebels unveil manifesto.
newsitem.headline: Mexican leftist rebels unveil manifesto.

text.p: Mexico's leftist Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) guerrillas have issued a manifesto in which they call for the refounding of the nation, the nationalisation of banks and a return to communal ownership of agricultural land.

In a "Proposal for the Nation" made available to Reuters late Tuesday, the group, which first appeared in June this year, said the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) had lost all legal legitimacy and should be overthrown by political struggle, of which armed opposition was a part.

"The biggest problem which we have in Mexico is political, and its origin lies in the breakdown of the rule of law produced by the government for the benefit of grand capital," the EPR said, in the most complete statement yet of its political and economic views.
The EPR has carried out attacks on police and military units in recent months in which at least 25 people have died.
It said recently though that it is currently concentrating on propaganda rather than military actions.
The movement said that while it was not against "financial capital" in and of itself, it had to be "subordinated, placed under control and regulated as a function of the Mexican people's needs".
"The national economy should be planned as a function of the interests of the majority of Mexicans," the EPR said.
"The banking system should be nationalised...the ejido (traditional communal landholding), communal property and small landholdings should be recovered."
Roads, railways and communications media should also become "the property of the nation", it said, although in an apparent contradiction it said it would not allow monopolies.

Former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari, who governed from 1988 to 1994, privatised Mexican banks and altered the constitution to reform the ejido system and allow greater private investment in the agricultural sector.

The EPR called for the overthrow of Salinas' successor President Ernesto Zedillo, whose government it accused of massive human rights abuses, and said a constituent assembly should be called to draw up a new constitution.
Zedillo has called the EPR a "terrorist" organisation and has pledged to hunt down its members "with the full force of the State."
